subject: Model Depot Alliance: access tiers, connector requirements, and MOU
messages:
From: Elena Kovács <elena@modeldepot.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Intro: ModelDepot partnership proposal

Hi Jonas / Camila,

Thanks for the quick intro, Camila — glad to meet you both. ModelDepot is an open model publisher focused on mid‑size conversational models and domain adapters. We9d like to explore a distribution alliance: Redwood surfaces our models to your customers via a catalog/connector, and we handle weights distribution and ongoing publisher support.

High level asks from our side:
- Clear access tiers (preview/embargo/public) so we can protect pre‑release work.
- Audit logs for downloads and attribution metadata preserved in the manifest.
- A simple rev‑share model for commercial usage; prefer revenue split over flat fees.
- Signed weights delivery (S3 presigned URLs) or signed escrow depending on customer risk profile.

We9ve attached a short partnership overview (MD-Partnership-Overview.pdf) that includes our proposed tiers and examples. Happy to hop on a short call to align. Proposed times: Tue/Thu next week, US morning.

Best,
Elena
Elena Kovács
Head of Partnerships, ModelDepot
attachments: MD-Partnership-Overview.pdf

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Kovács <elena@modeldepot.ai>
Cc: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: ModelDepot partnership proposal

Elena — thanks, this is helpful.

Quick clarifying items before scheduling a wider sync:
1) We need to confirm redistribution rights for downstream customers (especially cloud marketplace scenarios). Does ModelDepot permit redistribution under a commercial license when customers bring their own infra via Redwood Private?
2) For embargoed releases: what is your expected duration and conditionality (e.g., embargo lifts on GA or specific milestones)?
3) Escrow vs presigned URLs — what metadata do you require recorded with each download (hashes, purchaser id, license snapshot)?
4) Operational: preferred mechanism for automated connector updates (S3 manifest + checksum vs API endpoint for model metadata)?

I9ve attached a quick draft MAP template to capture milestones and responsibilities (Draft-MAP-template.docx). Camila / Sergio — can you review and propose an initial SOW for a 90‑day pilot? Laura, can you flag any legal/regulatory blockers you anticipate here?

If that all sounds good, Elena — would you do Tue 2026-02-16 15:00 PST (23:00Z) or Wed 2026-02-17 09:00 PST?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
attachments: Draft-MAP-template.docx

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T10:22:00Z
Subject: Internal: ModelDepot — proposed access/ops structure

Team — jotting a quick internal note based on Elena9s deck and Jonas's questions. High level proposal we can present back: 

- Access tiers: 
  * Preview: invite-only, token‑capped evals (max QPS and token limits), no redistribution.
  * Embargoed partner: S3 presigned weights, signed MOU, audit logging (download + usage), access tied to customer contract and MPN.
  * Public listing: model packaged for general availability with clear licensing; CDN distribution optional.

- Licensing: prefer a two‑track approach — OSS‑permissive variants remain CC/Apache as published; commercial weights (fine‑tuned or adapters) use a rev‑share/marketplace fee. We offer attribution metadata in catalog entries.

- Ops/connector: initial connector integration via manifest + presigned S3 under a per‑release manifest that includes checksum (sha256), semantic version, and license tag. For larger models we can support streaming pull via signed APIs.

- Pilot scope (90 days): 1 GA‑like customer (preselected), instrumentation for download & token usage reports, one production bugfix window / monthly review.

Sergio — can you draft the SLA bullets (uptime for connector, support window, rollback semantics)? Laura — we9ll need a short checklist for SOC/SLA fit. I9ll handle the partner ops onboarding plan.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Kovács <elena@modeldepot.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-20T16:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: ModelDepot partnership proposal

Jonas / Camila,

Thanks for the thoughtful breakdown — apologies for the delay. A few clarifications inline: 

> redistribution rights for downstream customers

We are comfortable with redistribution to end customers who have an explicit commercial license or are covered under the customer's Redwood contract. For marketplace redistribution we require a separate reseller addendum (standard for our licensed weights).

> embargo duration

Typical embargo is 60–120 days depending on the release. We9d be open to a conditional lift on GA + agreed benchmarks.

> metadata recorded with downloads

We ask for: download timestamp, downloader email/company id, manifest version, and sha256 checksum. Audit logs can be delivered weekly via secure S3 bucket with read‑only IAM role for ModelDepot legal.

> connector update mechanism

Presigned S3 + manifest is fine; we also support a webhook that notifies us of a new manifest version.

I9ve attached a rough license draft (MD-License-terms-draft.txt) and I9ll push an MOU to DocuSign if the SLA bullets align. We9re also open to a revenue share in the 5–15% range — exact split depends on channel responsibilities.

Cheers,
Elena
attachments: MD-License-terms-draft.txt

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Kovács <elena@modeldepot.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-24T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: ModelDepot partnership proposal — SLA and pilot proposal

Elena — appreciate the clarity. Attaching an initial Connector SLA (Connector-SLA-v1.pdf) with the following high‑level asks from Redwood: 
- Integrity: manifest + sha256 checksum verification required before model load.
- Delivery: presigned S3 URLs for initial pilot; escrow option if customer requires third‑party custody.
- Support: 24x5 email support for pilot; 8x5 engineering on‑call for critical P1s with 2hr response SLA.
- Telemetry: weekly token usage + download logs; support for an audit export on request.
- Security: KMS encryption for keys at rest; RBAC for manifest publishing.

Commercial ask for pilot: 90‑day pilot with a 10% revenue share for paid usage during pilot, then review. We9ll open a Jira (ALLIANCES-2124) to track work items and propose a kickoff next week.

Next steps: Elena — if you9re OK with these bullets I9ll send a DocuSign MOU and the legal teams can work the redlines. Camila / Jonas — let9s lock a kickoff for Wed 2026-03-03 16:00 CET / 07:00 PST.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Alliances
Redwood Inference
attachments: Connector-SLA-v1.pdf
related: JIRA ALLIANCES-2124

Sergio / Jonas / Camila,

Thanks — we9re happy to proceed. Our legal team signed a clean MOU and I attached the signed PDF (MD-MOU-signed.pdf). A couple tiny redlines came back on marketplace reseller language; nothing major. We accept the 90‑day pilot, agree to the telemetry bites noted, and confirm the 10% pilot rev‑share.

We9ve scheduled a kickoff for Wed 2026-03-03 16:00 CET / 07:00 PST and I9ve sent the DocuSign link to the contacts listed in the MOU. Please confirm the internal kickoff invite and we9ll circulate the pre‑kickoff playbook (integration checklist + manifest schema).

Best,
Elena
Elena Kovács
Head of Partnerships, ModelDepot
